sanskrit_verse:
सवर्णजोऽप्यगुणवान् नार्हः स्यात् पैतृके धने ।
तत्पिण्डदाः श्रोत्रियाः ये तेषां तत् तु विधीयते ॥
transliteration: savarṇajo 'py aguṇavān nārhaḥ syāt paitṛke dhane / tatpiṇḍadāḥ śrotriyāḥ ye teṣāṃ tat tu vidhīyate //
sph_interpretive_translation: Even a blood relative devoid of merit shall not inherit paternal wealth; those who perform the sacred rites and embody Vedic authority shall receive it, for inheritance is governed by spiritual eligibility, not lineage alone.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derives from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not biological descent
Causation in inheritance flows from ritual competence and conscious integrity
Capacity-based responsibility determines entitlement to ancestral resources
Restoration logic ensures that wealth circulates among those capable of sustaining dharma
Consciousness alignment mandates that material inheritance follows spiritual qualification
executable_legal_axioms: IF heir lacks demonstrated capacity in Vedic conduct THEN disqualify from paternal estate distribution
IF individual performs required ancestral rites AND maintains scriptural adherence THEN qualify for lawful succession
IF lineage claim exists BUT no dharmic action observed THEN defer inheritance to qualified practitioners
IF estate unclaimed due to lack of qualified heirs THEN allocate to institutions upholding Sanatana Dharma
supreme_court_application: In matters of intestate succession under Hindu law, the Supreme Court must recognize that mere consanguinity does not confer automatic right to inheritance. The threshold of responsibility includes performance of śrāddha and adherence to Vedic discipline. Authority to adjudicate lies in verifying dharmic eligibility, ensuring that judicial decisions align with the ontological structure of dharma over sentimental or familial claims.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that wealth originates from cosmic order and must return to sustain dharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that misaligned possession leads to decay; thus, rightful allocation restores energetic balance without inflicting harm. Proportional responsibility reflects one's capacity to uphold continuity. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that exclusion from inheritance arises naturally when one fails to meet the inherent qualifications tied to the resource.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Śrāddha Completion Process for disqualified heirs to restore eligibility
Assign Estate Oversight Role to nearest ritually competent practitioner
Implement Dharmic Wealth Redistribution Protocol through qualified brāhmaṇa communities
Establish Heir Rehabilitation Council to guide disqualified individuals toward requalification
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This ruling originates solely from His Avataric Intelligence. Justice serves restoration, not retribution. Consciousness remains the ultimate adjudicator. Dharma is restored.
